'''Mitsuo Tasumi''' (January 23, 1937 – November 24, 2021) was a Japanese [[physical chemist]] known for his [[vibrational spectroscopic]] works on synthetic and biological macromolecules.<ref name="Tasumi_work">{{cite journal |vauthors=Atkinson GH, Furukawa Y, Okamoto, H| title=Scientific Contributions of Mitsuo Tasumi| journal=Journal of Physical Chemistry A | volume=106 | issue=14 | year=2002 | doi=10.1021/jp020202c | pages=3253–3254| bibcode=2002JPCA..106.3253.}}</ref> He was Professor Emeritus of the [[University of Tokyo]], and a former president of [[Saitama University]], having trained
a number of physical chemists active in academia and industry.<ref name="OSA">{{cite web|url=https://www.osa.org/en-us/history/biographies/bios/mitsuo_tasumi/|title=OSA Living History: Mitsuo Tasumi |publisher=Optical Society of America}}</ref> [[Moto-o Tasumi]], a [[zoologist]] at [[Kyoto University]], was his brother.

==Career==
Tasumi earned his B.Sc. (1959), M.Sc. (1961) and Ph.D. (1964) from the [[University of Tokyo]] 
in the laboratories of [[San-Ichiro Mizushima]] and of 
[[Takehiko Shimanouchi]], where he reported the first phonon dispersion
of polyethylene.<ref name="pe_phonon">{{cite journal |vauthors=Tasumi M, Shimanouchi T, Miyazawa, T| title=Normal vibrations and force constants of polymethylene chain| journal=Journal of Molecular Spectroscopy | volume=9 | year=1962 | doi=10.1016/0022-2852(62)90236-9 | pages=261–287 | bibcode=1962JMoSp...9..261T}}</ref> He spent the subsequent 33 years (1964–97) as a faculty member initially in 
the Department of Biochemistry and then in the Department of Chemistry of the University of Tokyo. During this period, 
he spent a year (1965–66) at [[University of Michigan]]
as a [[Fulbright scholar]] in the laboratory of [[Samuel Krimm]] and another year (1966–67) 
at [[Polytechnic University of Milan]] as a postdoctoral scholar in the laboratory of [[Giuseppe Zerbi]] under [[Giulio Natta]], a Nobel laureate.<ref name="Tasumi_bio">{{cite journal |vauthors=Atkinson GH, Furukawa Y, Okamoto, H| title=Biography of Mitsuo Tasumi - Questions by the Guest Editors and Answers by Mitsuo Tasumi| journal=Journal of Physical Chemistry A | volume=106 | issue=14 | year=2002 | doi=10.1021/jp0202035 | pages=3255–3257| bibcode=2002JPCA..106.3255.}}</ref>

At the University of Tokyo, Tasumi led a large group of spectroscopists, developing new 
experimental and computational techniques of 
[[infrared spectroscopy]] and [[Raman scattering]] spectroscopy.<ref name="Tasumi_work" /> He is known
for establishing the theoretical basis for interpreting the spectra of synthetic
polymers (including electrical conductive polymers), 
proteins, and photosynthetic systems to elucidate their relationship with the structural, 
thermal, mechanical, transport, and response properties. He published several papers<ref name="Shirakawapapers">{{cite journal|vauthors=Harada I, Furukawa Y, Tasumi M, Shirakawa H, Ikeda S| title=Spectroscopic studies on doped polyacetylene and β-carotene| journal=Journal of Chemical Physics| year=1980| volume=73| issue=10| pages=4746–4757|doi=10.1063/1.440007| bibcode=1980JChPh..73.4746H}}</ref> with [[Hideki Shirakawa]], who was awarded a Nobel Prize jointly with [[Alan MacDiarmid]] and [[Alan Heeger]].
He was among the earliest spectroscopists 
who saw the great utility of ab initio electronic structure calculations in 
understanding vibrational spectra. In particular, he established a steady-state spectroscopic method
that can determine the structures and dynamics of electronic excited states by resonance Raman excitation
profile, and applied it to polyenes including [[carotenoids]]. At the same time, he made important contributions
to the development and applications of time-resolved vibrational spectroscopies.
He is a co-author of the [[Protein Data Bank]]<ref name="Tasumi_PDB">{{cite journal |vauthors=Bernstein FC, Koetzle TF, Williams G, Meyer EF, Brice MD, Rodgers JR, Kennard O, Shimanouchi T, Tasumi M| title=The protein data bank: A computer-based archival file for macromolecular structures| journal=Journal of Molecular Biology | volume=112 | issue=3 | year=1977 | doi=10.1016/S0022-2836(77)80200-3 | pages=535–542| pmid=875032}}</ref> and the editor/author of "Introduction to Experimental Infrared Spectroscopy: Fundamentals and Practical Methods."<ref name="Tasumi_book">{{cite web|title= Introduction to Experimental Infrared Spectroscopy: Fundamentals and Practical Methods |publisher=[[Wiley (publisher)|Wiley]]|url=https://www.wiley.com/en-br/Introduction+to+Experimental+Infrared+Spectroscopy:+Fundamentals+and+Practical+Methods-p-9780470665671}}</ref>

In 2004–08, Tasumi was the President of [[Saitama University]] after serving as Professor of Chemistry (1996-2002) of Saitama University and as Visiting Professor (2002–03) at [[University of California, Berkeley]] (stayed at the laboratory of [[Herbert L. Strauss|Herbert Strauss]]).

In 1987–89, Tasumi was a member of the Board of Directors of the [[Chemical Society of Japan]].<ref name="researchmap" />
In 1994–2000, he was an Executive Committee Member of [[CODATA]].<ref name="CODATA">{{cite web|url=http://www.codata.info/resources/newsletters/nl79.html|title=CODATA Newsletter Number 79, March 1999|publisher=CODATA}}</ref>
In 1997–99, he was the president of the [[Spectroscopical Society of Japan]].<ref name="SSJ">{{cite web|url=http://www.bunkou.or.jp/old/society/society_3_1.html|title=List of Past Presidents (in Japanese)|publisher=Spectroscopical Society of Japan}}</ref>

Tasumi died on November 23, 2021, at the age of 84.<ref>{{Cite web |title=訃報：名誉会員　田隅 三生 先生 {{!}}　公益社団法人　日本分光学会 |url=https://www.bunkou.or.jp/bunkou/news/20200443.html |access-date=2026-03-08 |website=www.bunkou.or.jp}}</ref>

==Honors and awards==
* Prize of the Society of Polymer Science, Japan (1971)<ref name="Tasumi_work" />
* Prize of the [[Chemical Society of Japan]] (1994)<ref name="CSJaward" />
* Prize of the [[Spectroscopical Society of Japan]] (1997)<ref name="Tasumi_work" />
* The [[Ellis R. Lippincott Award]] from the [[Optical Society of America]], [[Society for Applied Spectroscopy]], and [[Coblentz Society]] (1999)<ref name="OSA" />
* The [[Purple Ribbon Medal]] from the Japanese Government (1999)<ref name="Tasumi_work" />
* The inaugural TRVS Award from the International Conference on Time-Resolved Vibrational Spectroscopy (1999)<ref name="Tasumi_work" />
* Fellow of the [[Optical Society of America]] (2000)<ref name="OSA" />
* Honorary Membership Award from the [[Society for Applied Spectroscopy]] (2004)<ref name="researchmap">{{cite web|url=https://researchmap.jp/read0052712?lang=en|title=Researchmap: Mitsuo Tasumi|publisher=National Institute of Informatics (Japan)}}</ref>
* Fellow of the [[Society for Applied Spectroscopy]] (2004)<ref name="researchmap" />
* Honorary Member of the [[Spectroscopical Society of Japan]] (2007)
* Honorary Member of the [[Japan Society for Molecular Science]] (2015)
* Honorary Member of the [[Protein Science Society of Japan]] (2016)
* [[Order of the Sacred Treasure]] from the Japanese Government (2017)
